rv.q: That said, this is largely a joyous show.
Buy The Play That Goes Wrong tickets in expectation of giant belly laughs, and you won’t be disappointed.

Nevertheless, I laughed a lot at this gloriously preposterous and utterly silly evening, and it’s lovely to see the fringe Mischief Theatre, founded in 2008 by graduates of LAMDA as an impro comedy troupe, make it to the West End by dint of sheer hard work and talent.
The production is a technical triumph: ensuring that props and sets collapse on cue, without actually injuring anyone, is a genuine feat of stage management.
But it is essentially a one-joke piece and the joke wears thin long before the end.

Still, there are laughs to be had here, and the production is a technical triumph: ensuring that props and sets collapse on cue, without actually injuring anyone, is a genuine feat of stage management.
It’s not sophisticated and it’s certainly over-extended; the show’s one-act Fringe origins aren’t hard to spot.
By the end, the house was roaring its collective head off.
All in all, it's a great-looking, brilliantly performed piece that is a lot more than a poor man's Noises Off.
The material is uneven: the first half is definitely stronger than the second, and it would benefit from losing 15 minutes.
One of the best nights out in London
That Goes Wrong will keep going wrong for quite a while. It has a brilliant formula and it earns every laugh.

cn.t: Critics find this farcical play-within-a-play delivers consistent laughs through meticulously choreographed chaos, though some note it lacks the depth of genre predecessors like Noises Off. A crowd-pleasing formula executed with precision.
